nodes.intent: Run one approved real-repository task through the proven Minimal Pool Runtime
nodes.change_spec: Parameterize the fixture-bound Pool Proof composition with a small reviewed task manifest containing the target repository path, immutable base commit, change specification, acceptance criteria, allowed changed paths, verification commands, exact model, and execution bounds. Reuse the public Minimal Pool Runtime, fresh Worker launch, sandbox, persistence, and cleanup paths without repository-specific branching. This node proves one approved Agent Pool repository task and does not add decomposition, full CRAFTS, grading tiers, GitHub automation, or production-release claims.
acceptance_criteria: A strict reviewed manifest can run one approved Agent Pool repository task through createMinimalPoolRuntime without fixture-specific runner branches
The task starts from the pinned base commit, uses a fresh isolated Worker and sandbox, and produces at most one commit touching only allowed paths
Malformed manifests, mutable revisions, path escapes, credentials, unknown fields, and unbounded commands fail before model work
Runner-owned evidence records the manifest identity, attempt/result IDs, selected model, process outcome, commit, cleanup, and bounded diagnostics without changing retained Pool Proof reports

nodes.intent: Submit a direct task and observe one durable real Worker result
nodes.change_spec: Add the smallest production composition root that connects the existing authenticated POST /tasks adapter and direct-task validation to SQLite work import, a SQLite-backed pending-task claim loop, one ready Minimal Pool Runtime slot, and bounded status queries. The path accepts caller-authored direct tasks only, preserves criteria and idempotency, launches the generalized runner, and records terminal status. It must not invoke decomposition, Gate 1, a separate durable queue service, full CRAFTS, Tier-2 grading, or GitHub delivery.
acceptance_criteria: An authenticated POST /tasks request persists one accepted direct task and returns a stable submission/work identity; replay with the same caller/key/payload returns the original identity
A SQLite-backed claim loop dispatches the persisted task to one fresh Minimal Pool Runtime Worker and recovers pending work after process restart without Redis or BullMQ
The direct path cannot invoke decomposition or Gate 1 and exposes bounded submission, attempt, and terminal-result status
A service-level test submits one approved real-repository task and observes its runner-owned terminal result without manual ledger edits

nodes.intent: Independently verify arbitrary approved task results
nodes.change_spec: Generalize the fixture verifier into a runner-owned deterministic verifier driven only by the reviewed task manifest and stored attempt identity. Verify process success, base/result commit relationship, allowed paths, clean repository state, caller-approved verification commands, and result uniqueness, then persist a structured pass/fail result with bounded evidence. Do not add model judging, CRAFTS phase grading, empirical thresholds, transcript object storage, or integration re-verification.
acceptance_criteria: A result passes only when the launched Worker identity matches, the expected commit descends from the pinned base, changed paths are allowed, the tree is clean, and every approved verification command succeeds
Worker prose cannot override a failed command, wrong commit, dirty tree, out-of-scope path, duplicate conflicting result, timeout, or missing evidence
The verifier emits and persists one bounded structured verdict linked to submission, work, node, attempt, result, manifest, base commit, and result commit identities
Deterministic tests cover pass, command failure, identity mismatch, commit mismatch, path violation, dirty tree, timeout, and conflicting-result outcomes

nodes.intent: Expose a verified task as a human-reviewable branch and PR-ready artifact
nodes.change_spec: For a deterministically passed direct task, preserve its verified commit on a named local review branch and emit a PR-ready markdown/JSON artifact containing intent, acceptance criteria, changed files, verification commands, verdict, and stable identities. A human can inspect or manually push/open the PR. Failed tasks expose bounded failure context and never produce a mergeable review branch. GitHub credentials, automatic PR creation, webhooks, connected-component assembly, comment continuation, and cryptographic Gate 2 records remain deferred.
acceptance_criteria: A passed task produces one local review branch pointing at the independently verified commit and one bounded PR-ready artifact with traversable evidence identities
A failed, timed-out, dirty, conflicting, or unverifiable task produces no mergeable review branch and exposes bounded failure context through status
Branch and artifact creation are idempotent for the same accepted result and reject conflicting replays

An end-to-end test covers authenticated direct submission through fresh Worker execution, deterministic verification, local review branch creation, and human-readable output without GitHub credentials
